body: The same molecule can be expressed in multiple, syntactically distinct representations, yet it remains unclear whether large language models (LLMs) can recognize and relate these equivalent encodings. We introduce MolReps, a pipeline that generates 9,600 question-answer pairs across ten representations for conversion, normalization, and 2D structure recognition. Post-training on MolReps improves text-only and multimodal models, MolQwen3-4B-Instruct (MQ3-4B-I) and MolQwen3-VL-4B-Instruct (MQ3-VL-4B-I), from 4.01% to 75.13% and from 7.11% to 73.14% (InChIKey match) on the molecule-overlap test set, respectively. On the molecule-disjoint test set, post-training increased validity from 20.35% to 58.12% for MQ3-4B-I and from 17.19% to 59.34% for MQ3-VL-4B-I. However, InChIKey match remained low, decreasing from 3.86% to 3.09% and from 6.44% to 2.29%, respectively. Furthermore, the resulting models achieve a relative 27.84% improvement in average over their base model on MolRepBench, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating molecular property prediction. These results show the effectiveness of targeted post-training for enhancing molecular representation understanding and its potential to improve downstream molecular tasks.
